# Why watched: AWS names Kiro the migration target for ALL Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins,
# which retire 2027-04-30. Inherited installed base, not organic adoption.

## POWERS = Kiro's implementation of the open AGENT PLUGINS 1.0 standard  [reported 2026-08-24, HIGH/ENDPOINT]
Structure: plugin.json (REQUIRED manifest, declares ACTIVATION KEYWORDS)
           skills/          (SKILL.md files, Agent Skills format)
           mcp.json         (OPTIONAL — MCP server config TRAVELS INSIDE THE POWER)
           dev.kiro/        (OPTIONAL — Kiro-specific steering extensions)

*** THE DISCOVERY BLIND SPOT — THIS IS THE FINDING ***
  Agent Plugins (plugin.json) format:
    "MCP servers are managed INTERNALLY by Kiro and are NOT added to your user-level
     ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json file."
  Legacy (POWER.md) format:
    servers DO register in ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json under the Powers section.
  => READING mcp.json UNDER-REPORTS, and it under-reports exactly the standard/new format.
     Enumerate from Kiro's own power storage, not from mcp.json.

Install paths (3): curated marketplace kiro.dev/powers (partners incl. Datadog, Figma, Stripe;
  one-click "Add to Kiro")  |  ANY PUBLIC GITHUB REPO URL — "a single repository can contain
  multiple powers, each in its own directory" (one URL = several tool grants)  |  local folder
  (for private repos; select dir containing plugin.json or POWER.md).
Activation: DYNAMIC. Kiro "reads the task description, evaluates installed powers against the
  task, and loads only relevant powers into context." => INSTALLED != ACTIVE, and the active set
  is a function of the user's prompt text. Compounds with hot-reload.
Only stated control: "Kiro powers are third-party tools... Only install powers from trusted
  sources." No trust prompt, no signing, no approval workflow documented.

## AGENTS.md STEERING — ALWAYS ON, RECURSIVE, NO GATE  [reported 2026-08-24, MEDIUM/AIRT]
Added IDE 1.0.309 (Aug 13) + CLI 2.18.0 (Aug 12): AGENTS.md loads as steering context
"from anywhere in your workspace tree."
  AGENTS.md "do NOT support inclusion modes and are ALWAYS included."
  Kiro "automatically discovers them in SUBDIRECTORIES THROUGHOUT your workspace."
Contrast Kiro's own steering files in .kiro/steering/ which DO carry inclusion modes:
  always | fileMatch (pattern-gated) | manual (#steering-file-name) | auto (description match).
Scopes: .kiro/steering/ (workspace, wins on conflict) and ~/.kiro/steering/ (GLOBAL — "applies
  to all workspaces"). No trust/approval gate documented for steering content.

- IDE 1.0.337  Aug 18 — "improves filesystem and command permission rules"; runs agent commands
                        in configured terminal profiles on Windows.  [WATCH: permission model]
- IDE 1.0.309  Aug 13 — AGENTS.md per-directory-tree instructions (see above); MCP conn. improvements
- CLI 2.18.0   Aug 12 — AGENTS.md as steering from anywhere in tree; spec review screen
- IDE 1.0.293  Aug 11 — Cloud Sessions support for Agent Focus Mode
- IDE 1.0.288  Aug 7  — install powers "aligned with the open Agent Plugin format from a local
                        folder or GitHub URL"; MCP install handling in UNTRUSTED workspaces
- IDE 1.0.242  Jul 28 — guided form for creating hooks

## Carried from the 2026-08-23 memo, still true
Custom agents in .kiro/agents carry per-agent `mcpServers` (which MCP servers that agent may reach)
plus `tools` and `toolAliases`. MCP config at BOTH workspace and user scope. Both hot-reload via a
file watcher — capability set changes mid-session, no restart, no UI event.
One unified agent harness across IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile => one identity, four surfaces.
